claims.statement: The root `build` script is the fan-out `pnpm -r run build`; every workspace package declares `"build": "tsdown"` with tsdown as its own devDependency (not a root one), emitting ESM into the package's `lib/` with `dts: true`, `clean: true` and `fixedExtension: false`.

A package that declares `dsh.client` builds through `clientBundle(id, libEntry)` in `scripts/tsdown.client.ts`, which returns three tsdown configs in emission order — the node half (owner of `clean: true`), the browser bundle pinned to `lib/client.js` as CJS with the `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` banner and `clean: false`, and a declarations-only pass (`dts: { emitDtsOnly: true }`) that produces `lib/client.d.ts`.

The client preset moves the runtime contract "registration id equals package name" into the build: `workspacePackage(id)` searches `packages/*/*/package.json` for a manifest whose `name` is exactly `id` and throws otherwise, so a stale id fails the build instead of emitting a bundle no boot-graph row can claim; `PLATFORM_MODULES` is the single copy of the shell seed table that `moduleTableWords()` and the `deps.neverBundle`/`alwaysBundle` predicates derive from, and `clientPurityPlugin` turns inlining another plugin's browser half into a build error.

`scripts/run-gates.ts` owns three validated aggregates — `check-all`, `hygiene` and `doc-sync` — and the root package scripts are only aliases of them (`gates`, `gates:hygiene`, `gates:doc-sync`); `check-all` currently schedules 11 gates and includes a `node --test .github/issue-management/policy.test.mjs` gate for the issue policy engine.

Only the two gates that read build artifacts — `package-exports` and `client-bundle-id` — declare `needs: ['build']`; `bundle-entries`, `publish-guard`, `export-jsdoc`, the three doc-sync gates and `issue-policy` are dependency-free leaves, no gate uses `after`, and although `check-all` passes `hygieneLeafGates({ artifactNeeds: ['build'] })` that option is not consumed, so `export-jsdoc` does not wait for the build.

`runGates()` validates the graph before any child process starts: an empty graph, duplicate gate id, a `needs`/`after` entry naming an unknown gate, or a dependency cycle (reported with the full cycle path) throws instead of letting the scheduler stall.

Gate scheduling separates ordering from success: a gate starts when every `needs` predecessor has `passed` and every `after` predecessor has merely settled; a pending gate whose `needs` predecessor failed or was skipped is recorded as `skipped` with `durationMs: 0` and an `error` naming the failed dependencies, and the aggregate exits 1 whenever any gate with `allowFailure !== true` is `failed` or `skipped` (no current gate sets `allowFailure`).

A gate counts as passed only when the child exited 0, was not killed by a signal, and did not fail to spawn; failure reporting keeps the three independent facts (spawn error, exit code, signal) from hiding each other.

Gate concurrency defaults to `min(gate count, min(4, availableParallelism()))` for every aggregate because several documentation gates each build a full parse/`ts.Program` workload, `DSH_GATE_CONCURRENCY` overrides it (must parse to a positive safe integer, otherwise the runner throws) and the startup line prints the worker count with its source, while `DSH_GATE_VERBOSE=1` additionally prints the captured output of passing gates.

The runner must be started through `pnpm run`: `pnpmScript`/`pnpmExec` resolve pnpm's executable from `npm_execpath` via `pnpmInvocation()` and throw when it is absent, and each gate is spawned shell-free with the repository root as `cwd`, merged `gate.env`, stdin ended, and stdout/stderr captured unless `streamOutput` is set.

The root vitest config discovers two test sources — `packages/*/*/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx}` and `scripts/tests/**/*.spec.ts` — so the `test` gate (root `test` = `vitest run`) runs the gate scripts' own tests in the same pass as package suites, and no per-package vitest config exists.

The root vitest config exists to remove three failure modes: workspace packages are aliased to their TypeScript sources with exact-match regexes because their published `./client` faces are type-only projections an object-form alias would swallow by prefix; `react`, `react-dom` and the JSX runtimes are pinned to the copy resolved from `packages/client/ui-memo/package.json` so a hoisted ReactDOM 19 cannot mismatch React 18; and `standardDecorators()` pre-transforms files containing `@Identifier` syntax so `@Remote` services run under test, with jsdom opted in per file via `// @vitest-environment jsdom`.

`verify-package-exports` asserts that every declared export target resolves on disk — `default` and `types` for each subpath, plus the root `main`/`types` fields — with no exclusions, including the declarations of a package that ships a bundled `dsh.client` face; it reads the emitted layout, so it must run after the build.

`verify-client-bundle-id` reads each `dsh.client.platform === 'web'` package's built `./client` bundle and asserts that the `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` registration id equals the package name, that every literal `require` is answerable from the module table (platform baseline plus `inject` plus `external`), that no non-literal `require` exists, and that every declared row resolves to an installed package which itself declares `dsh.client` (subpaths judged by owning package).

`verify-bundle-entries` enforces that each composition entry id has exactly one owning bundle: a patch inserting the same id twice always fails, two different bundles inserting one id fail unless both patches record the exclusion with the `not both` marker plus the bare id, and a documented overlap is reported rather than failed; the gate states its own limit — it can only see bundles this repository ships.

`verify-publish-guard` requires that any manifest declaring a `workspace:` range in one of the four dependency fields run `scripts/publish-guard.mjs` as `prepublishOnly` and that the named path resolve to the repository's own guard file; it reads manifests only, so it verifies the wiring rather than observing a publish, and the guard itself is what blocks a non-pnpm packer.

`verify-export-jsdoc` builds a read-only `ts.Program` over `packages/*/*/src/**/*.ts` (falling back to `skipLibCheck`/`noLib` compiler options because the repository has no root `tsconfig.base.json`), requires parameter and non-void-return documentation on exported functions, public class members, namespace members and inline callable types plus description prose on exported declarations, exempts protocol slots, constructors, inherited contracts and source re-exports, fails closed on unclassifiable forms, and restricts itself to the names reachable through `exports` for packages that do not export `src/*`; since it reads source, it declares no build dependency.

`verify-translation-pairing` treats a README as a three-file pair (`README.md`, `README.zh.md`, `README.i18n.yaml`): the metadata file records the git blob hashes of both sides with CRLF normalized to LF, and the check requires matching hashes, a language switcher linking each side to the other, and identical structure signatures (heading levels, code-fence count and info strings, table row counts, list types), with `--write` re-recording and `--list` reporting state.

`verify-md-links` and `verify-md-wrap` share `scripts/markdown.ts` and `scripts/repo-files.ts` and scan only repository-authored READMEs, `AGENTS.md` files and `.agents/skills/**/*.md` (excluding archived agent notes and deduplicating symlinks): links and images must resolve to existing targets, a `#fragment` onto Markdown must match a GitHub heading slug or explicit `<a id>`, and a prose paragraph must occupy a single physical source line, with the wrap gate masking VitePress frontmatter and `:::` delimiters first.

Gate scripts are themselves tested from `scripts/tests/`, but those unit tests deliberately pin only parsing and resolution rules while workspace-wide artifact assertions stay inside the gates — because `lib/` is build output absent from a clean checkout, a global unit assertion would fail on any machine that had not built yet, which is what allows `test` to run before `build`.

A gate must not guard its own fix: the issue-policy workflow checks out `policy.mjs` from the default branch, so a policy fix cannot be validated on the pull request that introduces it and must land on `main` first, and the general rule is to fix the subject instead of weakening a gate to make it pass.

CI's only verification job installs with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and then runs `pnpm run gates` — the same aggregate used locally — so the local-first rule applies (the whole suite green before a pull request, never pushing a red gate for CI to discover), while separately path-filtered workflows re-run the translation-pairing and issue-policy checks as faster feedback rather than as additional authority.

Adding a gate takes two edits — a `verify-*` script in the root `package.json` plus a `pnpmScript()` entry in `gatesForMode()` carrying `needs: ['build']` only when the gate reads artifacts (with `pnpmExec()` and `nodeGate()` covering tool execution and `node --test` forms) — after which `AGENTS.md`'s command list and gate count must be updated to match.
